coverage: targeted, non-exhaustive; same-day boundaries separately logged

new_fulltext_audits.title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Wang, Ziyong and Lin, Yupei and Huang, Runxuan and Lin, Liang and Zhang, Dongyu and Wang, Guangrun
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: Secs. 3-4; Tables 1-3; main methods and experiments; no separate appendix found
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: 93.8% mean is below N0-VTLA 96.2%; title does not establish overall superiority. InsertHole ablation changes online touch and demonstration-derived tactile references together. No hardware validation of descriptor availability.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: A frozen GPT-6 Astra controller uses scene/wrist images, proprioception, bilateral tactile images, pooled indentation-depth descriptors, marker displacements, and interaction history. Offline task skills and tactile references are distilled from 40 demonstrations plus ten validation episodes per task; this is not a demonstration-free policy. Generic inverse kinematics executes bounded action segments. Across five UniVTAC tasks and 500 simulator episodes, mean success is 93.8%, above N0-TWAM's 84.6% but below N0-VTLA's 96.2%, contrary to an unqualified reading of the title. A paired InsertHole comparison reports 99% with touch versus 31% without, using identical initial configurations, controller, and action budget. However, the intervention removes both online tactile information and tactile reference material and changes the modality-matched skill description. Depth and marker descriptors are deformation proxies, not independently validated force measurements. The evidence supports a powerful reference-conditioned simulated controller and a task-specific benefit of the tactile-information bundle, not a universal model ranking, isolated online-touch effect, physical force understanding, real-time hardware control, cross-sensor robustness, or held-out contact-topology generalization.

new_fulltext_audits.title: Learning Tactile-Aware Hand Representations from Human Hand-Object Interaction Data
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Yu, Yeonguk and Kim, Jaehong and Han, Byungok
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: Secs. III-V; Tables I-IV; Fig. 4; methods, evaluation and limitations
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Human proximity pseudo-contact is not tactile force. Leave-one-object-out is object OOD, not topology OOD. Sparsh-Skin comparison involves target fine-tuning and architectural differences, not zero-shot cross-sensor deployment.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: HuTact pretrains hand representations on 2.57 million human interaction frames using wrist-local fingertip coordinates and mesh-distance pseudo-contact, not measured human touch. Separate coordinate and tactile tokenizers, hand/finger positional structure, and spatial-then-temporal Transformers transfer to Revo2 sensor channels through tokenizer reinitialization and downstream adaptation; optional robot-play midtraining adds 44 minutes. Episode-level splits precede temporal-window construction. Grasp Macro-F1 improves from 88.23 to 93.29; leave-one-object-out grasp performance improves from 74.92 to 80.27, with substantial object-level variability. With only 25% of grasp labels, the adapted model reaches 88.26, comparable to full-label scratch training. Two real manipulation tasks use 40 trials each: ACT and Diffusion Policy both average 50% success with the pretrained representation, versus respective no-touch baselines of 33.8% and 22.5%. Scratch tactile encoders score 32.5% and 38.8%. These results support transferable initialization and data efficiency. They do not isolate all architectural versus data-source effects, demonstrate zero-shot sensor transfer, or establish contact-topology generalization; the Sparsh-Skin comparison fine-tunes a differently structured source model on the same target platform.

new_fulltext_audits.title: Embodied Task Agents Can Perform Fine Manipulation through Tactile In-Context Learning
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Wang, Yubang and Huai, Zezheng and Zhang, Yifei and Wu, Jinhao and Chen, Yitong and Zhang, Haozhe and Li, Sixian and Gong, Jingjing and Lin, Zhenyang and Chen, Ziyang and Qiu, Xipeng
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: Secs. 3-5, Tables 1-3; Appendices A, B, D, E, F; selected qualitative cases in C
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Simulation isolates demonstration touch while current touch remains available. Real comparison adds an entire multimodal demonstration, not touch alone. 60 Hz command execution is not 60 Hz model feedback; real trials are only five per condition per task.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: Tactile-ETA supplies a frozen embodied model with action-aligned demonstrations containing before/after vision, proprioceptive motion, and synchronized tactile strips. A change-based selector retains endpoints and salient adjacent frames without force or slip labels. In the main simulator comparison, current visual, tactile, and execution feedback are held constant; only demonstration tactile information changes. Across four tasks with 100 matched initializations each, mean success rises from 15.75% to 24%. On LiftBottle, selected tactile frames reach 36%, versus 27% for endpoints or no demonstration touch and 2% for all frames, indicating that temporal presentation matters. More demonstrations are not monotonically better: one, two and four shots average 22.5%, 24% and 19%. Two physical tasks achieve three successes in five trials each with a human multimodal demonstration versus zero without; that real comparison does not isolate touch. Control commands execute at 60 Hz, but inference occurs between bounded motion segments and simulation pauses during reasoning. Evidence therefore supports contextual tactile information and compression, not continuous low-latency control, robust real-world reliability, sensor invariance, or topology OOD.

new_fulltext_audits.title: GPT-6 Astra Is a Native Visuo-Tactile Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Yang, Chen and Shi, Linzhe and Zhang, Hang and Xu, Mu and Fan, Jiansheng and Wang, Chen
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: Secs. 3-8; Tables 1-5; Appendices A-B protocol details
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Published baseline comparisons use different evaluation subsets; GraspChip success was relaxed relative to the native benchmark. Four tasks worsen with touch. Median 14 s API latency is incompatible with calling the model a 60 Hz controller.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: TacTalent wraps frozen GPT-6 Astra with scene vision, bilateral tactile images, proprioception, bounded history, and one to three successful demonstrations. End-effector and gripper commands execute through a fixed controller. Nineteen simulator tasks span UniVTAC and OpenViTac; matched vision-only and vision-plus-touch conditions use 210 scene seeds per modality, normally ten trials per task. Reported suite means with touch are 93.8% and 81.8%, versus 76.3% and 80.6% without touch. Six tasks improve, nine tie, and four deteriorate, so the result is not a uniform tactile advantage. Comparisons with published learned-policy baselines do not use identical evaluation subsets. Moreover, GraspChip uses a relaxed success rule that accepts supported intact placement without the original release/withdraw requirement. Demonstration selection, benchmark-specific criteria and small per-task samples matter when interpreting the high success rates. The paper reports approximately fourteen-second median vision-tactile API latency; sixty-hertz command execution is not a model feedback rate. No physical experiments, held-out sensor/embodiment tests, topology-defined splits, repeated-model-seed confidence analysis, or controlled tactile-texture masking experiment establish broader deployment claims.

new_fulltext_audits.title: Touch Where It Matters: Learning Local Tactile Policies for Fine-Grained Gripper Control
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Ba, Mingyuan and Zhou, Yanan and Zhao, James and Zhi, Weiming
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: Secs. III-IV; Eqs. 1-8; Tables I-III; main methods and experiments
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Independent local policies are not an explicit cross-hand/contact graph. Full system runs local gripper control at 60 Hz versus baselines at 30 Hz; measured success cannot isolate representation from timing/routing/auxiliary losses.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: ContactPolicy separates visual arm motion from local tactile gripper control. Each arm independently encodes bilateral fingertip image differences, sensor-reported three-axis forces, arm position/velocity and gripper state; it predicts a gripper increment and apply/hold modulation. A visual intention selector switches stages, while future tactile-latent and force prediction are training-only auxiliaries. Six physical tasks, five bimanual, use fifty demonstrations and twenty-five evaluation trials per task. Overall success is 124/150, or 82.7%, versus 57.3% for multimodal fusion and 42.7% for vision-only control. However, local gripper updates run at 60 Hz while baseline policies run at 30 Hz, so the system comparison bundles control frequency, routing, context and auxiliary supervision. Across three tasks, arm-state conditioning raises successes from 43 to 63 out of 75 and reduces premature failures from 22 to five, supporting contextual gating. The evidence demonstrates useful real local tactile feedback in coordinated tasks, not an explicit interhand contact graph, isolated representation superiority, calibrated force invariance, held-out topology generalization, or robust cross-embodiment transfer. Evaluation remains within the demonstrated task/platform setting.

new_fulltext_audits.title: ACTS: Learning Visuo-Tactile World Models from Human Physical Interaction
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Ma, Yuxiang and Xu, Weihan and Ye, Pengfei and Mei, Anna and Song, Yuxin Ray and Li, Tingle and Chen, Haonan and Adelson, Edward H.
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: Secs. 3-7; Tables 1-3; Appendices A-I, especially force calibration, action conditioning, splits and metrics
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Predictions condition on entire future recorded sensor-motion/estimated-force windows. Pixel metrics use VAE-reconstructed targets; robot tactile persistence wins PSNR on five of six streams. No control-success or calibrated force-dynamics validation.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: ACTS trains object-specific multiview world models on 4.91 hours of bimanual human interaction and evaluates transfer on fifteen robot episodes without robot training. GelSight images, wrist/scene views, OptiTrack poses and tactile-derived normal-force estimates supply five synchronized streams and force-augmented actions. Critically, predictions receive the entire recorded future action window, including future measured sensor motion and estimated force. This supports offline trajectory-conditioned prediction, not deployment-observable forecasting from current sensing and prospective commands alone. An eight-frame history predicts eight future frames, about 0.53 seconds. Human scene PSNR improves over a scratch baseline, but comparisons also differ in pretraining and, for ContactWorld, context length and stream decomposition. Metrics use VAE-reconstructed targets; static gel appearance can dominate them. On robot tactile streams, copying the latest frame wins PSNR on five of six streams, while ACTS improves LPIPS on five. A separate calibration study reports 0.318 N force-estimation MAE, not manipulation-force or shear ground truth. The evidence does not establish contact-timing accuracy, causal physical understanding, closed-loop planning success, sensor transfer, or topology OOD.

new_fulltext_audits.title: Ego2Contact: Predicting Touch from Egocentric Human Video for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Yang, Qianqian and Li, Dayou and Liu, Bangya and Zhu, Zihao and Chen, Nuo and Xu, Siyuan and Hu, Hezhen and Yu, Chen and Friesen, Rebecca and Zheng, Minghui and Hipwell, Cynthia and Qian, Xiaoning and Shimada, Kenji and Fan, Zhiwen
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: Secs. III-IV; Tables I-IV; real-world policy protocol and Fig. 6
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Robot transfer needs substantial target-domain adaptation; zero-shot robot IoU is 0.008. Real predicted touch is used offline for policy post-training, but evaluation supplies measured glove touch. No quantitative real success table supports sensorless real deployment.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: Ego2Contact predicts bilateral pressure/contact grids from egocentric video using global visual features, hand-local features and conditional flow generation. Anatomical regions and hand-aligned grids provide explicit structure, but not a relational contact graph. Human unseen-object contact IoU reaches 0.4812 versus TouchAnything's 0.4720, while volumetric IoU is slightly lower. Transfer requires target-domain adaptation: robot contact IoU rises from 0.008 zero-shot to 0.476 after substantial paired simulator training. Online predicted touch improves three simulated policy tasks modestly but remains far behind measured/simulator touch on precision tasks: pen-cap success is 0%, 1% and 95% with no, predicted and ground-truth touch. The real pipeline adapts with approximately 123,000 paired frames and uses predicted tactile features for offline policy post-training. During actual real deployment, however, the policy receives measured tactile-glove observations, not the video predictor. Reported real results are qualitative rather than a quantitative success-rate comparison. Consequently, the study supports adapted contact-field estimation and limited simulated sensor substitution, not zero-shot cross-sensor invariance, sensorless real manipulation, full force observability, or held-out topology generalization.

new_fulltext_audits.title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Chen, Tianxing and Lin, Wenwei and Lyu, Chuqiao and Xiang, Peicheng and Tang, Junyuan and Nian, Tian and Cai, Zijian and Ye, Kehe and Yu, Chenze and Zhu, Wenxuan and Chen, Eric J. and Qin, Yan and Chen, Yue and Wu, Tongyu and Gong, Junhao and Lei, Kai-Chong and Zhang, Jiahao and Su, Kailun and Liang, Qiwei and Xu, Renjing and Luo, Ping and Ding, Wenbo
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: Secs. 3-6; Tables 1-4; Appendices A-G and Tables 5-11; PDF p.9 Tables 2-3 visually verified
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: 44→52% real success isolates retaining tactile information in pretraining, not online touch, since both variants use touch downstream. Ego Humanoid transfer includes target fine-tuning. Same glove family is not a cross-sensor test; no topology-defined OOD.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: Spark-0 pretrains a vision-language-action system with 1,000 hours of human tactile recordings and spatial alignment losses. Training-only depth geometry and projected hand-contact maps supervise visual latents; online tactile force histories and spatial pressure tokens enter the action expert rather than the language backbone. A matched-RGB, matched-compute ablation compares visual-only pretraining with retaining tactile information. On the vision-only Ego Humanoid evaluation, after target fine-tuning, success improves from 52.45% to 71.72%; this is adapted embodiment transfer, not zero-shot deployment. On five real tactile-enabled tasks, success rises from 44% to 52%, based on ten trials per task. Both variants use touch during downstream training and deployment, so the contrast isolates pretraining information rather than online tactile sensing. Simulation success barely changes, from 36.57% to 36.86%. Every method fails full completion of the real Insert Test Tubes task despite nonzero partial scores. The same glove family on human and target robot, one reported training seed, and limited real trials leave sensor invariance, uncertainty, physical force accuracy and held-out contact-topology generalization unresolved.

new_fulltext_audits.title: GRASP: Global-Local Representation Alignment and Spatial-Physical Grounding for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Ren, Zeyuan and Zhao, Guanxun and Li, Qi and Wang, Hao and Liao, Wenlong and Luo, Keyi and Zhang, Xijing and Zhang, Zhiyuan and Cui, Jingye and Gu, Qibin and Wang, Zhichen and Hu, Yucheng and Xia, Liqiao and Bu, Nan and Ma, Zhengde and Li, Rankun and Yang, Xue and Xie, Wende
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: III-A/B; IV-A/B; IV-C Table I; IV-D Fig. 4; V
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Kinematic rather than contact-force grounding; no topology-held-out test.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: GRASP injects forward-kinematic TCP and inter-arm relative-pose losses plus future DINOv3 feature and Grounding-DINO region supervision during training. Runtime retains learned queries, current multi-view RGB, instruction and robot state, not future frames or teachers (III). The five pi0.5 variants share demonstrations, initialization and training-step budgets. RoboTwin evaluation uses 50 tasks, 50 demonstrations/task and 100 episodes/condition (IV-A/B). Clean/randomized success is 64.13/36.15% for baseline, 79.22/52.84% for full GRASP, and 68.30/65.15% for query-only; the full method therefore loses randomization robustness relative to query-only. TCP mean error falls from 5.3 to 4.6 mm (Table I). Hardware covers four tasks with about 150 demonstrations/task, five training seeds and 30 trials/checkpoint; success requires intervention-free completion and error bars describe across-seed SD. Juice-making improves from 56.7% to 83.3% (IV-D). Reviewer inference: useful bimanual/tool-use prior comparison, but grippers, no tactile observations, detector-dependent supervision, and one hardware platform limit claims about dexterous contact structure or force/load transfer. new_fulltext_audits.title: CQDC-Warp: GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Quasi-Dynamic Simulation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Ding, Yanchen and Chen, Jiayi and Xu, Jianfeng and Zhao, Wei and Yi, Li and Wang, He
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: IV; V-A/B; VI-A Table II; VI-B; VI-C/D Table III; VII
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: GPU-batched versus CPU-sequential speedup is not a matched-hardware comparison.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: CQDC-Warp combines compliant contact, implicit dynamics derivatives and sampled geometry derivatives for local MPC. Inputs include scene/robot models, current configuration, goals, suitable initialization and robot links intended to contact objects; dynamics choose realized geometry/friction, not an externally prescribed mode schedule (IV-V). On 17 Allegro objects with 1,024 trials/object, success is 79.8% versus CFree 73.7% and IMPACT 65.2%; trajectory times are 0.794, 21.422 and 39.844 seconds. These timings compare 1,024 GPU worlds against single-core sequential baselines (VI-A, Table II). Removing geometry derivatives reduces success by 2.44 points; horizon ablation also matters (VI-D). Bimanual Shadow bottle opening and shared-object lifting succeed in 1,024/1,024 and 1,007/1,024 trials. Hardware only replays a scanned-bottle/table trajectory on Sharpa at fivefold slower duration, without closed-loop tactile validation (VI-B). Reviewer inference: include as contact-mechanics/planning evidence, not learned tactile representation or deployed bimanual transfer. Initialization/contact-intent assumptions, task-family tuning, and unevaluated downstream data-learning benefits constrain interpretation. No seeds/confidence intervals or held-out contact-topology protocol are established.

new_fulltext_audits.title: DexGraspFlow: Topology-Aware SE(3) Flow Matching for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasp Generation
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Zhou, Bin and Ma, Boyu and Zhou, Xinyu and Dong, Jiahua and Zhou, Chuhao and Liu, Yizhou and Wan, Hao and Yang, Jianfei
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Finger-removal kinematic OOD is not a held-out dynamic contact-graph protocol; retain historical 0/30.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: Dual-stream flow matching models link-link and link-object relations, with URDF shortest-path biases and geometric features; Pyroki IK recovers joints (3). Training uses 14,011 grasps on 48 objects across Barrett, Allegro and Shadow; ten objects are held out. Success means object displacement within 2 cm after six directional perturbations. With 3,000 trials, mean success is 95.33% versus TRO-Grasp 94.60%; same-GPU single-sample latency including IK is 0.132 versus 0.257 seconds (4.1-4.2). Geometry-only/topology-only/no-bias success is 89.70/92.73/86.63% (Table 4). Seven unseen finger-removal variants produce 88.74% versus DRO 53.11% and TRO 20.47% over 7,000 trials/method. This genuinely changes kinematic links, but is not a learned contact-participant/edge holdout (4.3). Real execution uses separately trained Linker-Hand demonstrations, RGB-D/FoundationPose, IK and added closure offsets: 91/100 lifts, not zero-shot novel-embodiment transfer (4.6). Seeds/uncertainty are not reported. Reviewer inference: valuable structural/morphology evidence; tactile sensing, bimanual coordination, contact-topology transfer and general novel-hand transfer remain unproven. Feasibility is delegated to IK rather than enforced during flow.

new_fulltext_audits.title: Physical Canvas: A Vision Tactile World Model For Robot Policy Evaluation And Learning
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Xing, Zebin and Zheng, Yuhang and Zheng, Yupeng and Zhang, Yichen and Li, Zichen and Zhou, Shangqing and Zang, Yujie and Liu, Yuchen and Xia, Zhongpu and Li, Haoran and Zhang, Qichao
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: 3; 4.1-4.5 Tables 2-4; Appendices A-H; B Table 5; E Table 6
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Task outcome correlation is not calibrated dynamics; no topology-defined OOD split.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: PhysCanvas jointly renders three RGB views, optical tactile images, marker displacements and task state through a shared Wan video model; FK/camera-projected command images condition dynamics. Training-only future targets and frozen scene/modality/state reward models provide supervision, including human-labeled real completion states (3; E). Four bimanual tasks cover handover/table reorientation/insertion, cap unscrewing, block separation and restricted cube turning. Data contain 3,805 training and 320 held-out rollouts (B). ACT/FM/pi0.5 receive current RGB, robot state and tactile displacement; imagined evaluation starts from real observations, then uses generated futures (D/F). EVAC/Open-Sora/WoVR comparisons assess visual metrics; staged ablations assess tactile MAE, timing and event F1. State supervision raises mean task-wise policy-outcome correlation 0.602→0.885; pi0.5 real success rises 59.1→70.8% after imagined RL. Evaluation uses three batches of 20 scenes/task-policy; policy results report three-run population SD (4). Event F1 falls 0.4550→0.4455 when modality consistency is added. new_fulltext_audits.title: PhantomTac: Hijacking Robotic Tactile Systems with Deploy-and-forget Tags
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Zhang, Binbin and Zhang, Yifeng and Chen, Xiaomeng and Chen, Dongyao
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Proposed consistency defense is not quantitatively validated; scope is magnetic sensing.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: PhantomTac supplies physical robustness evidence rather than a new manipulation policy. Controlled laboratory interventions corrupt magnetic tactile force estimates, disrupting feedback on a Dofbot gripper and Unitree G1 contact task (6). An interference-free 20-trial grasp baseline succeeds throughout; offset robustness tests use 20 trials per direction/distance and report greater than 95% attack success within the tested 8 mm bound (6.2/6.4). Response-model blind tests report approximately 0.16 N RMSE, but this evaluates sensor-response prediction, not calibrated manipulation uncertainty (5.1). Multiple commercial sensor models show susceptibility, with differing response magnitudes; model-specific characterization is needed (6.5/7.2). The proposed independent proprioceptive consistency monitor is a defense discussion, without a measured defense benchmark (7.1). Reviewer inference: supports evaluating whether represented contact is physically trustworthy and cross-modally corroborated. It establishes neither bimanual/load-transfer competence nor universal tactile vulnerability: optical, capacitive and resistive sensors are outside direct scope. The official abstract claims CCS 2026 acceptance and lists DOI 10.1145/3830454.3846657; publisher verification failed. No code execution or independent reproduction was performed.

new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Load sums tactile-estimated force magnitudes, not independently measured net wrench.

new_fulltext_audits.title: No Eyes, No Problem: What Does Touch Contribute to Blind Baoding Ball Manipulation?
new_fulltext_audits.authors: Deshmukh, Ayush and Agarwal, Nalin and Miller, Elle and Vijayakumar, Sethu
new_fulltext_audits.evidence_locator: III-A-E; IV-A-B; V/Table II; VI-A-C; VII
new_fulltext_audits.coding_note: Same-checkpoint tactile-off supports runtime tactile dependence; separately trained proprio-only has different slew scale. 112.5-rotation showcase is outside ten-trial statistics. One ball pair, no held-out contact topology.
new_fulltext_audits.audit_summary: A four-frame proprioceptive/binary-touch policy controls one Shadow Hand Lite and two balls at 60 Hz, with hardware-aligned coupling, calibration and episodic sensor corruption (III). Ten hardware trials/configuration give 34.75 mean full rotations versus 5.00 when touch is zeroed in the same checkpoint (IV-V/Table II). The 112.5-rotation showcase is separate from these statistics. Simulation aggregates 768 episodes over three seeds; hardware uses one ball pair. The separately trained proprioception-only policy differs in slew-rate setting, so it is not a clean sensing-only comparison. Sensor corruption plus slew limits transfer better than the intermediate controller, but a cumulative ladder does not isolate all interactions. This strengthens a compact binary-feedback baseline and runtime-ablation requirement, not a claim for richer representations, independent load estimates or held-out contact-topology transfer. Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not performed.
